raised: The page doesn't say whether to buy the S&P 500 in an investment savings fund or a securities account
No numbers to compare: no fees, tax amounts, lock-up periods or past returns
Top-menu items ('questions everyone asks', 'investing in an index') pull the reader away from the page
The 'two parts' section uses מק"מ and אג"ח before explaining them
The small grey line saying product pages list what you can invest in is easy to miss
Card titles in the everyday-money section are cut off
Can't tell how the comprehensive new pension fund differs from the general new pension fund
The 'contributions and personal severance' card is incomprehensible
The self-selection section doesn't say which option suits someone like the reader
The index cards read almost the same as each other
Only the retirement cards have a 'plain language' line; the reader wanted one on every card
The 'daily' and 'renewing' chips on the money market card are unclear, including whether they are buttons
Every index card ends with the same repeated phrase about dollar exposure
'Deposits above the maximum amount' is unclear: what maximum, and does it apply to the reader?
'Dollar exposure or hedged': no guidance on which is better
Unexplained difference between the S&P 500 card ('in dollars') and the MSCI World card ('in shekels')
Jargon: 'weighted by market value', 'public holdings with a cap per share'
'After a period set by law' doesn't say how long
No information on risk or how much money can be lost
Doesn't say what the reader already has through work and what they'd have to open themselves
No order of steps after the three 'where to start' lines
No information on how to actually open a product or who to contact
Would drop the 'for children' section
Would drop the Tel Aviv index cards and most of the MSCI/Nasdaq cards as near-duplicates
Would drop the 'what the site doesn't cover yet' section
Would drop the everyday and short-term money section
Would drop the 'contributions and personal severance' and general new pension fund cards

problems.why: The reader mentions reading the 'general track' card only because their pension might be in one, and never objects to it being listed as an exposure.
